question: Should OpenClaw adopt Discord source-message subagent progress as a supported opt-in product surface, including seven configuration controls and the new shared delivery-context/channel-lifecycle contracts?
rationale: The patch is technically credible, but code review cannot decide whether this visible Discord feature and its permanent public/configuration surfaces belong in the supported product contract.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in surface
options.body: Approve the Discord feature and shared contracts, then require a conflict-resolved exact-head refresh with upgrade and restart proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to existing progress UI
options.body: Reuse or extend Discord progress drafts and status-reaction infrastructure while avoiding a parallel lifecycle contract and broad new configuration surface.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Close the PR and leave source-message subagent progress outside OpenClaw's supported Discord product surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the opt-in surface
recommendation.body: Approve the Discord feature and shared contracts, then require a conflict-resolved exact-head refresh with upgrade and restart proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily concerns supported Discord user experience and configuration, with agents/hooks owners available to confirm the shared contract shape.
